paragraphs: Augintel builds software for health and social services agencies whose staff are buried in paperwork. The product pulls narrative data out of case notes, forms, and records and centralizes it. The pitch is that a worker can review an entire case history in minutes instead of reading the file page by page.

Natural language processing identifies the critical content inside those notes. A case dashboard reveals clinical risks described within notes and maps how those risks progress over the life of the case. Supervisors, quality specialists, and executives can customize a dashboard of quality indicators and alerts across an agency. Frontline staff see risks, strengths, and social determinants surfaced automatically. Alerts for early warning can be customized by the agency.

Caseworkers, clinicians, supervisors, and executives are the intended users. The company describes its team as specialists in natural language processing, a subdiscipline of artificial intelligence that uses computers to understand the written word. Its algorithms were trained with the help of partner agencies to understand the context of social services. Marty Elisco is listed as CEO and chairman of the board.
